family.description: Exploratory re-measurement of the transpose/conversion family: gf2's canonical 64x64 word transpose against M4RI mzd_transpose and Bitshuffle bshuf_bitshuffle (kernel-isolated, preallocated output), and the whole-consumer BitMatrix::transpose at 63x63, 64x64 and 65x65 against M4RI's fresh-output mzd_transpose and against Bitshuffle through a measured geometry adapter (row padding to a multiple of eight, byte packing, plane unpacking; the copies are skipped where the canonical and Bitshuffle layouts coincide, so the 64x64 consumer pays no copy). The baseline arm is always the established gf2 route and the candidate is always the external arm, so the speedup of medians is median(gf2)/median(external) and a value above 1 means the external arm is ahead; `improved` in a comparator-gap cell is a material gap in the external arm's favour that needs attribution and `regressed` means gf2 is materially ahead. Unpadded Bitshuffle at 63 and 65 rows is unavailable (element count must be a multiple of eight) and is not substituted. The family's v3 pilot and confirmation ran gf2 arms that reported `warm` without the protocol's untimed pass over the working set before calibration, so their gf2 `warm` declarations are false and their comparisons are withdrawn. This campaign re-measures every cell of the v3 pilot addendum with fixed gf2 arms that make that pass (timed_windows in dev/active/6fb89a3c/survey/gf2-side/src/lib.rs). Protocol v3 allows one confirmatory attempt per candidate identity and version; the withdrawn confirmation's ledger reservation holds the identity of every external candidate these cells use (bitshuffle-transpose, m4ri-transpose). The executable of bitshuffle-transpose is unchanged. m4ri-transpose's warm pass in the committed receipts transposed each input into a fresh output, leaving the kernel cell's preallocated output outside the pass; the fixed arm's warm pass runs the timed call on every bank (dev/active/6fb89a3c/survey/m4ri_transpose_arm.c). Its executable changed from sha256 651915b3cf3abef44e54bbecd8fd4a75560d2443960e75b9cc8344fbf7ba0b37 to 5cdd572ebf07455d13bd3c627af447a8d75654e69012b37f1a8e10ea38ab84f0: a new candidate identity for the same comparator whose confirmatory attempt the withdrawn confirmation spent, and this family opens no confirmatory attempt with it. Every cell here is therefore exploratory and no interval carries a confirmatory decision. Pilot trials per cell, counting every committed campaign that started a pilot of this question under protocol v1 (family transpose-vs-external-pilot) or v3 and this campaign: transpose-64-canonical-vs-m4ri 6, transpose-64-canonical-vs-bitshuffle 5, transpose-consumer-63-vs-m4ri 5, transpose-consumer-64-vs-m4ri 4, transpose-consumer-65-vs-m4ri 4, transpose-consumer-64-vs-bitshuffle-adapter 3, transpose-consumer-63-vs-bitshuffle-adapter 2, transpose-consumer-65-vs-bitshuffle-adapter 2. The search budget declares the maximum, within the protocol cap of 8; the earlier v3 addenda counted v3 trials only. Workload seeds expand through SplitMix64 [Steele2014], implemented as tuning_campaign_support::abtest::SplitMix64 (dev/tools/tuning-campaign-support/src/abtest.rs) in the gf2 arms and as splitmix64_next (dev/active/6fb89a3c/survey/harness_common.h) in the C arms; both are pinned by the producing snapshot. This survey adopts no production implementation; no cell here decides adoption.

effect.rationale: Comparator-gap cells only. This survey adopts no production implementation, so no worthwhile-speedup threshold applies and none is declared.
effect.equivalence_rationale: The one-sided non-inferiority margin the withdrawn confirmation froze; exploratory cells record decisions under it and never pass.
effect.material_gap_rationale: Material-gap threshold 1.2: a 20% gap in a nanosecond-scale transpose is the smallest difference worth attributing to a named cause (tile kernel, allocation, partial-word handling, geometry conversion) rather than to host noise; it is the threshold the withdrawn confirmation froze.

complexity_budget.maintenance_rationale: The family surveys external comparators and changes no production code; the whole diff is under dev/.
